edge.title: The deposit that isn't in a bank
edge.anchor: The Times of India reports a Bengaluru woman's ₹3 lakh FD at a credit co-op society matured in 2020 and a forum has ordered a refund, with 9.5% interest and ₹35,000 compensation, after six years of waiting.
edge.setup: A neighbour recommends a 'co-operative' that pays about a point more than bank FDs, with a neat receipt, a friendly office near the market and a name that sounds like a bank. You can open the FD in ten minutes with a cheque. Nothing about it looks different from the branch you already use.
edge.tell: The name on the receipt says 'society' or 'credit co-operative', not a bank licensed by the RBI.
move: Before depositing, check that the institution is a licensed bank, not a society. Look it up on the RBI's list of banks.
If it is a society, treat the money as unprotected by the bank deposit insurance and put in only what you could wait years to recover.
Keep the receipt and pay by cheque or transfer. If maturity is refused, complain in writing early and ask where a consumer or co-operative registrar complaint can be filed.
edge.why: A higher rate is the price of weaker protection, but the receipt looks the same either way, so the risk is invisible until maturity. The check is about what the institution is, not how it looks or how many neighbours use it. It works on any deposit scheme.
edge.variants: Same shape: the chit fund with a registered-sounding name, the 'nidhi' that offers monthly interest, the builder's 'deposit scheme' sold as an FD.

lens.name: Selection effects
lens.one_line: How a group got assembled usually explains the result better than anything about its members.
lens.detail: A survey of app users can't tell you about people who deleted it. Hospital data on a disease overrepresents severe cases, because mild ones never came. Online reviews over-sample the delighted and the furious. Before accepting a comparison between two groups, the first question is always how each group came to be in the sample.
elsewhere: 'Our customers love us' — the unhappy ones already left.
Exam toppers from a coaching centre that only admits toppers.
Crime statistics shaped by which complaints get registered.
lens.test: How did these people end up in this group — and who never had the chance to?
lens.today: A Bengaluru woman's ₹3 lakh FD at a credit co-operative society matured in 2020, and a consumer forum has only now ordered a refund with 9.5% interest and ₹35,000 compensation (The Times of India). We hear about the depositors who kept pursuing it for six years; those who gave up never show up in the story. That makes the visible recoveries look like the typical outcome when they are not.

moved.what: Hoteliers in Bengaluru are weighing price revisions after the ₹8-per-litre milk price hike (The Times of India).
moved.so_what: Expect tea, coffee and tiffin to cost more from November. If you eat out daily, add the higher figure to your monthly budget now.

moved.what: The Bengaluru–Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper starts public service on 3 November (Deccan Herald), with a 19:45 departure via Pune, Solapur and Kalaburagi (RailJournal).
moved.so_what: If you are planning a Mumbai trip, compare this overnight service's fare and timing against flights before you book. Confirm the date on IRCTC, as earlier reports gave 1 November.

moved.what: The Pink Line's 7.5-km stretch has safety clearance. Udayavani reports a 15 November launch by the Prime Minister, while Goodreturns still asks whether it is likely.
moved.so_what: Treat 15 November as probable, not confirmed. Do not change a home or commute plan until BMRCL announces public opening.

moved.what: Karnataka restricts Deepavali fireworks to 20:00–22:00 on 8 to 10 November, and only green crackers are allowed (The Times of India).
moved.so_what: If you buy crackers, buy green ones and plan to light them in that window. Expect noise and smoke in the evening, so schedule evening travel and any pets or elders around it.

moved.what: The Bengaluru–Karwar Vande Bharat Express is to be launched by the third week of November (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: If you travel to the coast, wait for the announced timetable and fares before booking other transport for late November.

carry_over.prompt: A branch executive you know offers a special scheme that is not on the website and takes your cheque to 'process it internally': what is the tell?
carry_over.answer: Your money leaves your hands, but no entry appears under your name in your own bank app or statement.
